q: 1. Workability of concrete is measured by
explain: The slump test is the standard field and lab method used to measure the consistency/workability of fresh concrete.

q: 2. Specified compressive strength of concrete is obtained from cube tests at the end of
explain: By convention and IS code practice, the characteristic/specified compressive strength of concrete is defined based on 28-day cube test results, by which time hydration has developed most of the strength.

q: 3. The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement (1: 3 cement mortar cube) after 7 days test should not be less than
explain: As per IS specifications, a 1:3 cement-sand mortar cube of ordinary Portland cement must achieve a minimum compressive strength of 17.5 N/mm² after 7 days.

q: 4. The increase in the strength of concrete with time is
explain: Concrete strength gain over time follows a non-linear curve — rapid initially and gradually slowing down, not a straight line.

q: 5. The test conducted in the laboratory on the specimen made out of trial concrete mix is called
explain: A preliminary test is conducted in the laboratory on trial mixes before actual construction to determine and verify the proportions needed to achieve the required strength.

q: 6. The maximum quantity of aggregate per 50 kg of cement should not exceed
explain: As per general guidelines, the total quantity of aggregate (fine plus coarse) used per 50kg bag of cement should not exceed about 450kg for good quality concrete.

q: 7. The strength of concrete after one year as compared to 28 days strength is about
explain: Continued hydration over time increases strength beyond the 28-day value; typical long-term gain at one year is about 20-25% more than the 28-day strength.

q: 8. Poisons ratio for concrete
explain: As per this text, Poisson's ratio of concrete tends to increase as the mix becomes richer (higher cement content).

q: 9. Minimum grade of concrete to be used in RCC as per IS 456: 1978 is
explain: As per the (older) IS 456:1978 provisions referenced here, M10 was permitted as the minimum grade usable in reinforced cement concrete.

q: 10. The approx. ratio of the direct tensile strength to direct compressible strength test is
explain: The direct tensile strength of concrete is generally only about 1/10th (0.10) of its direct compressive strength, reflecting concrete's inherent weakness in tension.

q: 11. In concrete mix design, allowance for bulking of sand is necessary in case of
explain: Bulking changes the apparent volume of sand due to moisture, so a correction is required only when proportioning is done by volume (volume batching), not by weight.

q: 12. In concrete mix design, allowance for surface water carried by aggregate is necessary in case of
explain: Surface moisture on aggregate adds extra water to the mix and affects the effective water-cement ratio regardless of whether batching is done by volume or by weight, so an allowance is needed in both cases.

q: 13. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: The degree of grinding of cement, is called fineness
The process of changing cement paste into hard mass, is known as setting of cement.
The phenomenon by virtue to which cements does not allow transmission of sound, is known as soundness of cement.
The heat generated during chemical reaction of cement with water, is known as neat of hydration.
explain: This statement is incorrect: soundness of cement actually refers to its ability to resist volume expansion/change after setting, not to sound transmission — the two share a similar-sounding name but different meanings.

q: 14. Water required for M25 concrete per bag of cement, is
explain: As per the standard nominal mix proportioning tables referenced in this text, the water requirement per 50 kg bag of cement for M25 grade concrete is taken as 35 kg.

q: 15. The top diameter, bottom diameter and the height of a slump mould are:
explain: The standard slump cone has a top diameter of 10cm, bottom diameter of 20cm, and a height of 30cm, as specified by IS code.

q: 16. In slump test, each layer of concrete is compacted by a steel rod 60 cm long and of 16 mm diameter for
explain: As per the standard slump test procedure, each of the four layers of concrete filled in the mould is tamped 25 times with the standard tamping rod.

q: 17. According to I.S. : 456, the number of grades of concrete mixes, is
explain: As per IS:456, concrete mixes were historically classified into 7 grades based on specified compressive strengths (though modern codes list more, this classic reference lists 7).

q: 18. The preliminary test is repeated if the difference of compressive strength of three test specimens, exceeds
explain: If the compressive strength results of three specimens from a preliminary test vary by more than 15 kg/cm², the test is considered unreliable and must be repeated.

q: 19. The ratio of various ingredients (cement, sand, aggregates) in concrete of grade M20, is
explain: The nominal mix proportion traditionally associated with grade M20 concrete is 1 : 1.5 : 3 (cement : sand : coarse aggregate).

q: 20. The 28 days cube strength of mass concrete using aggregates of maximum size 5 cm for gravity dams should be
explain: Mass concrete for gravity dams using 5cm maximum size aggregate is typically specified to achieve a 28-day cube strength ranging between 150 to 500 kg/cm².

q: 21. The approximate ratio of direct tensile strength to direct compressive strength test of concrete
explain: Concrete is inherently weak in tension compared to compression; its direct tensile strength is only about 1/10th (approximately 0.10) of its direct compressive strength.

q: 22. The dimensions of a 35 liter forma for measuring aggregates by volume, are:
explain: A standard 'farma' (gauge box) with dimensions of 27cm × 27cm × 48cm gives a volume of about 35 liters, used for volumetric batching of aggregates on site.

q: 23. The minimum quantity of cement to be used in controlled concrete is specified is
explain: For controlled concrete mix design, the minimum cement content specified in this text is 220 kg per cubic metre.

q: 24. The concrete in which no preliminary tests are performed for designing the mix is called
explain: Ordinary concrete uses fixed nominal mix proportions without preliminary trial-mix testing, unlike controlled concrete.

q: 25. The controlled concrete is used for
explain: Controlled concrete mix design is applicable across the full range of seven grades of concrete specified in the code.

q: 26. Proper proportioning of concrete, ensures
explain: Correct mix proportioning of cement, aggregates, and water ensures all these desirable properties - strength, workability, durability, water tightness, and wear resistance - together.

q: 27. The workability of concrete by slump test is expressed as
explain: The result of a slump test is simply the vertical subsidence of the concrete cone, measured and expressed in millimetres (mm).

q: 28. As the grade of concrete increases the quantity of cement required per cubic metre
explain: Higher grade concrete requires higher compressive strength, which is generally achieved by increasing the cement content per cubic metre of concrete.

q: 29. Allowable shear strength of concrete, depends upon
explain: The allowable (permissible) shear strength value used in design is directly based on the concrete's own inherent shear strength characteristics.

q: 30. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following. While performing preliminary test on concrete
options: proportions of the material and water should be the same as to be used at the work site
cement should be mixed by hand in order to maintain uniformity
concrete mix should be stored in air-tight containers
concrete ingredients should be kept at a temperature of 37 deg +/- 2 deg C
explain: For preliminary tests, mixing should ideally be done as it would be at the site (usually by machine, not hand) to reflect actual site conditions; mixing by hand purely 'to maintain uniformity' is not the correct requirement, making this statement incorrect.

q: 31. Minimum number of test specimens required for finding the compressive strength of concrete are
explain: As per standard practice, a minimum of 3 test specimens (cubes) are cast and tested to determine the compressive strength of a concrete batch.

q: 32. For the construction of the retaining structures, the type of concrete mix to be used, is
explain: For retaining structures which require higher strength due to lateral earth pressures, a richer mix of 1:1½:3 (M20 grade) is typically used.

q: 33. The correct proportion of ingredients of concrete, depends upon
explain: Correct mix proportioning must account for all these factors - bulking of sand, water content, absorption of aggregates, and desired workability - to achieve an accurate and effective concrete mix.

q: 34. The following proportion of the ingredients or concrete mix, is not in confirmation to arbitrary method of proportioning
explain: In the arbitrary method, the standard nominal mixes follow ratios like 1:1:2, 1:2:4, 1:3:6, 1:4:8; the ratio 1:4:10 does not fit this standard arbitrary series.

q: 35. If X, Y, Z are the fineness moduli of coarse, fine and combined aggregates, the percentage (P) of fine aggregate to combined aggregates, is
explain: The formula for the percentage of fine aggregate needed to achieve a combined fineness modulus, based on the fineness moduli of coarse (X), fine (Y), and combined (Z) aggregates, is p = [(X-Z)/(Z-Y)] x 100.

q: 36. The bond strength between steel and concrete is due to
explain: The bond between reinforcing steel and surrounding concrete develops through a combination of both frictional resistance and adhesive chemical bonding at the interface.

q: 37. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following
options: workability of the concrete mix decreases with an increase in the moisture content
concrete for which preliminary tests are conducted, is called controlled concrete
bulking of sand depends upon the finesse of grains
concrete mix 1:6:12, is used for mass concrete in piers
explain: Workability actually increases (not decreases) with an increase in moisture content up to a point, since more water makes the mix more fluid and easier to work with, making this the incorrect statement.

q: 38. The concrete shrinkage is more pronounced in
explain: A rich mix contains a higher proportion of cement paste (which is the shrinking component), so shrinkage is more pronounced in rich mixes compared to lean mixes.

q: 39. Poisson's ratio of concrete reduced by using
explain: Using a richer mix (more cement content) tends to reduce the Poisson's ratio of the resulting concrete.

q: 40. For finding compressive strength of concrete, the minimum number of cubes required is
explain: As per standard testing practice, a minimum of 3 concrete cubes are cast and tested to determine the average compressive strength for a given sample.

q: 41. The value of vee bee time for low workability as per IS is prescribed as
explain: As per IS classification, low workability concrete corresponds to a Vee-Bee time of about 10 to 20 seconds.

q: 42. The 28 days cube strength of mass concrete using aggregates of maximum size 5 cm for gravity dams should be
explain: For mass concrete in gravity dams using large aggregate (5 cm max size), the required 28-day cube strength is relatively modest, typically specified as below 200 kg/cm², since strength requirements are lower than structural concrete.

q: 43. If the compacting factor of concrete is 0.90, then the workability according to IS is
explain: As per the IS classification table used in this text, a compacting factor of 0.90 falls in the 'low' workability category.

q: 44. The behavior of concrete under instantaneous loads is
explain: Under instantaneous (short-duration) loading, concrete behaves approximately as an elastic material, following a near-linear stress-strain relationship.

q: 45. The durability of concrete is due to its resistance to
explain: Durability of concrete is defined by its overall ability to resist deterioration from a combination of environmental exposure, internal disruptive forces, and chemical attack/cracking.

q: 46. In concrete, use of angular crushed aggregate in place of natural rounded gravel affects
explain: as per book c.Angular crushed aggregate provides better mechanical interlock and bond with the cement matrix, which particularly improves the flexural tensile strength of the concrete.

q: 47. Concrete can take tension up to
options: 10% of the compressive strength of steel
10% of the combined compressive strength of concrete & R/F
10% of the total tensile strength of the section
explain: Concrete's tensile strength is generally only about 10% of its own compressive strength, reflecting its characteristic weakness in tension relative to compression.

q: 48. The cube strength of concrete exceeds the cylinder strength by (in percent)
explain: Due to the difference in specimen geometry and the resulting confinement/end effects during testing, cube strength typically exceeds cylinder strength by about 20 to 25%.

q: 49. For cylindrical specimens, the dimension of cylinder generally used
explain: The standard cylindrical test specimen used for compressive strength testing has a diameter of 15 cm and a height of 30 cm, giving the standard height-to-diameter ratio of 2.

q: 50. Cube test is used to determine
explain: The standard cube test is specifically designed to determine the compressive strength of concrete, the most commonly required strength parameter.
